newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.S. raids on Iraq drag Karachi stocks to year-low.
newsitem.headline: U.S. raids on Iraq drag Karachi stocks to year-low.

text.p: Pakistani stocks dropped to a new year-low on Tuesday after the United States launched missiles on Iraq and brokers said the index could plunge further if the conflict is prolonged.
"The news of the U.S. attack on Iraq has dragged down the index," dealer Hina Akhlaq of KASB & Co said.
"It is yet more bad news for a market already depressed by political and economic uncertainty," dealer Ali Asghar of Fortune Security said.

The Karachi Stock Exchange 100-share index fell 6.91 points, or 0.49 percent, to end at a year-low of 1,412.96 points. The index, hit by political unrest and a troubled economy, has slid 435.35 points since its year-high of 1,855.22 on February 15.
It has lost 286.71 points since Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government unveiled a tough, deficit-cutting budget for 1996/97 (July-June) on June 13.

"People expected a small technical rally led by select blue chips including telecom utility PTCL and Hub Power today. The index opened firm, but plunged on news of the U.S. attack on Iraq," said dealer Sajjad Mankani of BMA Capiatal Managment.
He said trading volumes dwindled after the news hit the market. "Most players are now in a wait-and-see mood as they want to see the impact of U.S. attack."

Dealer Shakil Anwar of Amanullah Suleman Securities said any regional conflict could affect Pakistan. "Initially there was some nervousness in the market, but we are still unsure of how big the conflict is," he said. "There are fears that fuel prices will go up as a result of any conflict in the Gulf."

Dealer Mumtaz Kazmi of Global Securities the continued oil export embargo on Iraq meant there would be no major impact on international oil prices. "Only if the conflict is prolonged, would it bear some impact on the Pakistani economy," he said.
The U.S. military launched cruise missile strikes on air defence and communications targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday in reprisal for Iraqi attacks on Kurds in the north.
